No Way!!!!!” Dean shouted in the back seat of a car in a TikTok video touting her nominations. “NO WAY!!” she shouted again, slapping her friend on the leg as she (presumably) stared at the news on her phone. title: Google Maps expands Ask Maps with itineraries, list search, and appointment booking
summary: The update starts rolling out today.
body: TL;DR Google Maps Ask Maps adds itinerary creation, list search, and appointment booking. The update rolls out today, with some features available only in the US. Google is expanding Ask Maps to over 30 countries in Europe, including Spain, Germany, and the UK. Google Maps introduced Ask Maps to help casually answer questions using Gemini, and now it’s getting three new features that help you make an itinerary, search your lists, and schedule appointments. With air travel more unpredictable than ever, it’s likely more people will be hitting the road instead of taking to the skies this holiday season, so these upgrades come at a good time. Planning an itinerary with Ask Maps can cover an afternoon of hitting stores to finish up all your holiday shopping or a multiday trek across several states. No matter what type of trip you’re setting up, Ask Maps will put numbered pins on the map for each stop along the way. For long excursions, it can create a schedule for each day with recommendations and tips for every stop. After everything is set up, you can share the plans with others, or if you love seeing an itinerary on a page, export it to Google Docs.

title: Grammy Awards: All the Artists Who’ve Been Nominated in the Big 4 Categories in the Same Year
summary: Remarkably, 13 of these 17 artists are women.
body: When the nominations for the 69th annual Grammy Awards were announced on Monday (Nov. 16), Ella Langley became the 17th artist to receive nominations in each of the so-called “Big Four” Grammy categories – album, record and song of the year plus best new artist – in the same year. Remarkably, 13 of those 17 artists are women. How to account for that? Grammy voters seem to like to give extra encouragement to talented young women artists. Langley is the first country artist to be nominated in each of the Big Four categories since Bobbie Gentry in 1968, who was the first artist from any genre to achieve the feat. Three times in recent years, two artists achieved the feat in the same year. Billie Eilish and Lizzo both achieved the feat in 2020. Olivia Rodrigo and FINNEAS both achieved it in 2022. Chappell Roan  and  Sabrina Carpenter both achieved it in 2025. This has happened more often in recent years because the number of nominees in each of the Big Four categories has expanded. Until the Grammy ceremony held in 2019, there were generally five nominees in each of those categories. The upcoming 69th annual Grammy Awards, set for Sunday (Feb. 7), will mark the ninth year in…

summary: Google Calendar’s Speedy meeting update adds option for starting meetings later.
body: Credit: Andy Walker / Android Authority TL;DR Google Calendar users can now configure the event durations of their Speedy meetings. You can choose between starting five minutes later or ending five minutes earlier. The gradual rollout is starting today for Workspace customers, Workspace Individual subscribers, and users with personal Google accounts. It can be hard to find time in your day to relax when you have back-to-back meetings. With Google Calendar’s Speedy meetings feature, however, you can sneak breaks into your busy schedule by shortening the default duration of your event. This feature previously only let you end meetings early, but now you’ll have more choice over where you want to insert your break. Google is starting to roll out an update for Calendar’s Speedy meetings feature. This update will let the user choose whether new meetings start five minutes later or end five minutes earlier. You’ll also be able to set your default meeting buffer per calendar.

title: Morphe v2.3.0 update unlocks 1440p and 4K YouTube downloads that even Premium doesn’t offer
summary: The community-driven customization project also adds native offline downloads to YouTube Music.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR Morphe v2.3.0 brings native in-app YouTube downloads up to 1440p and 4K (2160p), surpassing official YouTube Premium’s 1080p cap. A new “Show download in video menus” setting adds download options to Premium-restricted videos, while downloads can now resume from their saved position and export directly to your device’s Downloads folder. YouTube Music gains native offline downloads that preserve SponsorBlock skips and more with this Morphe release. Morphe , the popular community-driven project based on prior work from ReVanced that lets users customize YouTube and other Android apps, has received a major v2.3.0 update that pushes offline capabilities beyond the 1080p quality official YouTube Premium subscribers get. The headline addition brings native in-app video downloads all the way up to 1440p and 4K (2160p), alongside an option to force these higher resolutions on older or lower-end phones that would normally be restricted.

title: Samsung’s Phone app could start checking if calls from contacts are being spoofed
summary: Use RCS-based caller verification, which first arrived on Pixels in June 2026.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung’s Phone app could soon warn you when a scammer is faking a call from your contacts. The feature uses RCS to verify that the call is indeed coming from the caller your phone says it is from. It does not share the caller’s details with Samsung’s servers, but will require an active internet connection. The feature will not verify calls coming from unknown callers, but only the ones saved in your contacts. In June this year, Google introduced a mechanism to identify potentially harmful spoofed or fake calls on Pixel devices . That way, a scammer using a spoofing tool to make the call appear to come from one of your contacts could be easily discovered. The feature works on RCS, the media-rich texting protocol that allows instant messaging on Google Messages, to match the call’s origin to the contact’s device. At the time of its release on Pixel phones, Google said it plans to expand it to other devices, and we’re seeing signs of that happening now, starting with One UI 9.5 on Samsung Galaxy devices.

title: Why you shouldn’t buy the latest flagship phone — and what to get instead
summary: Older flagship phones still pull their weight.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority Smartphone hardware is in an undeniably good place these days. While technological advancements continue apace, the difference they make to your day-to-day experience is increasingly about quality-of-life improvements rather than genuinely game-changing features. Longer software support has also taken some of the appeal out of regular upgrades. Our phones are now built to last five, six, or even seven years before we need to replace them. At the same time, average prices are creeping up , which is obviously always a good reason to keep an older handset ticking over for a little longer.

title: Bluetooth HDT could finally fix wireless audio quality, but there’s still one big problem
summary: HDT will be one of the biggest changes to Bluetooth audio in years.
body: News that Bluetooth has officially adopted its new High Data Throughput (HDT) specification should be music to audiophile ears far and wide. And there’s a good chance your future pair of wireless headphones could sound considerably better as a result. If you missed the announcement, Bluetooth HDT extends the capabilities of Bluetooth Low Energy (LE), boosting its maximum physical-layer data rate (PHY, pronounced “fie”) from 2Mbps to a comparatively colossal 7.5Mbps. That’s almost four times the maximum rate of conventional Bluetooth LE, and 2.5 times faster than Bluetooth Enhanced Data Rate (EDR), which tops out at 3Mbps.
